items.title: Developer Behind Mississauga's First Proposed AI Data Centre Signals It Will Fight the New Building Freeze
items.summary: According to the Kenora Miner & News, Mississauga council voted Wednesday to pause approvals for new data centre developments for at least twelve months, following more than five hours of debate and over 20 delegations from residents. The freeze grew out of concerns raised a month earlier at a packed town hall over the city's first proposed AI data centre, a roughly 220,015-square-foot facility that real estate firm Prologis wants to build at the northwest corner of Tenth Line West and Argentia Road. Residents pressed council on the project's water use, its draw on the electricity grid, air and noise pollution, and how densely computing hardware would be packed into the building, questions officials acknowledged they still don't have full answers to. Prologis had already worked through the city's Committee of Adjustment and Planning and Development Committee, where staff found the proposal generally consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and the Mississauga Official Plan. Despite that earlier progress, the outlet reports the company is expected to challenge council's new pause. The vote makes Mississauga the only municipality in Ontario to freeze new data centre approvals so far.

items.title: Charminar Indian Cuisine Back Open in Mississauga After a Health Inspection Shutdown
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Public Health temporarily closed Charminar Indian Cuisine, located at 5023 Spectrum Way, Unit B in Mississauga, after an inspection on July 31 turned up problems serious enough to warrant a shutdown. The restaurant has since reopened. The closure is part of Peel Public Health's ongoing inspection program, which routinely checks restaurants, cocktail bars and beverage rooms, bakeries and takeout establishments across the region for compliance with food safety standards. Mississauga.com notes the program exists specifically to give residents visibility into how local food establishments are performing on health and safety. For a business on Spectrum Way, the shutdown and swift reopening show how quickly an inspection can halt operations, and how fast a restaurant can address the issues to get back open. Anyone curious about a specific establishment's history can check Peel Public Health's public inspection records for more detail.

items.title: Facing a Tough Summer Job Market, Mississauga Teens Are Building Their Own Businesses Instead
items.summary: INsauga reports that youth unemployment across the Greater Toronto Area peaked at nearly 17 per cent in April, with the CNE alone receiving close to 50,000 applications for its job fair last week, making this a difficult summer for teenagers hunting for traditional work. Rather than compete for scarce openings, a growing number of Mississauga students are starting their own ventures through the city's Summer Company program, funded by the Government of Ontario for people between the ages of 15 and 29. One standout example the outlet highlights is Jobbli, an online student job board created by a Grade 10 student in Mississauga to help other young people find work. Thirteen students from this year's program will get the chance to showcase what they built at the IDEA Connect Summer Market at Square One Shopping Centre on August 12. INsauga notes participants receive training and hands-on guidance from IDEA throughout the summer as they turn their business ideas into functioning companies. For students who came up empty in a brutal job market, the program offers a different kind of summer income, one they built themselves.

items.title: Mississauga Becomes First GTA City to Move Toward a One-Year Data Centre Freeze
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city council voted unanimously on July 29 to direct staff toward preparing an Interim Control Bylaw that would freeze new applications for large data centres for up to a year. The motion, brought forward by councillors Martin Reid and Sue McFadden, targets facilities built for artificial intelligence, hyperscale computing and cloud services, an industry councillors say has grown faster than the city's existing planning rules can handle. During the freeze, staff would review land-use and environmental policies before recommending permanent regulations for the sector. Mississauga.com notes the move makes the city the first in the Greater Toronto Area to take this step, following months of public concern over the scale and impact of proposed data centre projects. Council is set to consider final approval of the bylaw at its September 16 meeting. Until then, the city's existing rules remain in place, but any new large-scale data centre proposal would face this pending freeze once it takes effect.

items.title: One of Ontario's Oldest Log Homes Marks 200 Years With a Streetsville Celebration
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says the Leslie Log House, built in 1826, is marking its 200th anniversary this year as one of the oldest surviving log homes in Ontario. According to the city, the milestone was celebrated with a special event bringing together members of council, city staff, representatives from the Streetsville Historical Society, and local heritage enthusiasts. The Leslie Log House is a designated heritage property that the city operates in partnership with the Streetsville Historical Society, offering visitors a look at daily life in early Upper Canada. City officials describe the site as an important reminder of Mississauga's rural and agricultural roots, predating the city's later suburban growth by nearly two centuries. Alongside the anniversary celebration, ongoing community programming at the site includes a tea room and art activities in the surrounding park. The city points residents to its website for further details on visiting hours and upcoming programming at the Log House.
